behaviours.title: Depositing into a never-opened account opens it and credits the amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'A' has never been opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance of 'A' is 100 and its entries are one deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected because the account was never opened, and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'unknown-account' and 'A' has no entries
the deposit is accepted but the balance is not readable until 'A' is opened explicitly

behaviours.title: Opening an already-opened account does not reset its balance or history
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the balance of 'A' stays 100 and it still has one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: re-opening resets 'A' to a balance of 0 with no entries
contrary_alternatives: re-opening throws an error saying the account already exists

behaviours.title: Balance of an unknown account reads as 0
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'ghost' was never opened
behaviours.then: the balance is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the balance is undefined because the account does not exist
contrary_alternatives: reading the balance throws an 'unknown account' error

behaviours.title: Entries of an unknown account are an empty list
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'ghost' was never opened
behaviours.then: an empty list is returned
behaviours.contrary_then: undefined is returned
contrary_alternatives: reading entries throws an 'unknown account' error

behaviours.title: Entries returned are a copy; changing them does not change the ledger
behaviours.given: account 'A' has one deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: the list returned by entries('A') is emptied by the caller
behaviours.then: reading entries('A') again still returns one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the ledger's history for 'A' is emptied as well
contrary_alternatives: the returned list is frozen and emptying it throws

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0 is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }, the balance of 'A' is 0 and 'A' has no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero deposit is accepted and recorded as a deposit entry of 0
contrary_alternatives: the zero deposit is silently accepted with no entry recorded

behaviours.title: A negative deposit is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative deposit goes through and the balance becomes 95
contrary_alternatives: the amount is treated as 5 and the balance becomes 105

behaviours.title: A deposit of NaN is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.when: NaN is deposited into 'A' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance of 'A' is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted and the balance of 'A' becomes NaN
contrary_alternatives: the deposit throws a type error

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to cents, with a half cent rounding up
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the balance of 'A' is 0.13 and the entry records an amount of 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent is dropped and the balance is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is stored unrounded as 0.125
the deposit is refused because it has more than two decimals

behaviours.title: Deposit fractions below half a cent are dropped
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the balance of 'A' is 1
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is kept unrounded and the balance is 1.004
contrary_alternatives: the amount is rounded up to 1.01

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId reports success but changes nothing
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: 100 is deposited into 'A' again with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 100 and 'A' still has one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is applied twice and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is refused with a 'duplicate' reason and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: An invalid amount is refused even when the txnId was already used
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeated txnId is recognised first and the result is { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the call is refused with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: A txnId used by a deposit makes a later transfer with the same txnId a no-op
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: 50 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, 'A' stays at 100 and 'B' stays at 0
behaviours.contrary_then: txnIds are tracked per operation type, so the transfer goes through: 'A' becomes 50 and 'B' becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is refused with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero withdrawal is accepted and recorded as a withdrawal entry
contrary_alternatives: the zero withdrawal is silently accepted with no entry

behaviours.title: A negative withdrawal is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes 150
contrary_alternatives: the amount is treated as 50 and the balance becomes 50

behaviours.title: A withdrawal reusing a seen txnId reports success without checking funds
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is checked on its own and refused with reason 'insufficient-funds'
contrary_alternatives: the call is refused with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: Withdrawing more than the balance is refused as insufficient-funds
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -50
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is paid out and the balance becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance is allowed and leaves 0
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 0 and the last entry is a withdrawal of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is refused with 'insufficient-funds' because it would empty the account, and the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is refused because a minimum balance must remain

behaviours.title: The funds check uses the amount after rounding to cents
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.then: the amount rounds to 100, the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the unrounded 100.004 is compared to the balance and the withdrawal is refused with 'insufficient-funds'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes -0.004

behaviours.title: Withdrawing from a never-opened account is refused and opens it empty
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where 'A' was never opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, the balance is 0 and entries('A') is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is refused with reason 'unknown-account'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -50

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of exactly 5000 is within the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and nothing has been withdrawn yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is refused with 'daily-limit' because the limit must not be reached, and the balance stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the daily limit is lower (e.g. 1000) and this withdrawal is refused

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 exceeds the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and nothing has been withdrawn yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: 5000 is paid out and the remaining 0.01 is refused

behaviours.title: Withdrawals accumulate towards the 5000 daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and 3000 has already been withdrawn with txnId 'w1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 7000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit applies per withdrawal, so it is accepted and the balance becomes 4999
contrary_alternatives: only the remaining 2000 of the limit is paid out and the balance becomes 5000

behaviours.title: Accumulated withdrawals reaching exactly 5000 are allowed
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and 3000 has already been withdrawn with txnId 'w1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is refused with 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 7000
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is refused because the total must stay below 5000

behaviours.title: A refused withdrawal does not use up any of the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and a withdrawal of 6000 with txnId 'w1' was refused for 'daily-limit'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the refused 6000 counted towards the limit, so this is refused with 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the account is locked for the day after a limit breach and every withdrawal is refused

behaviours.title: The daily limit is tracked separately per account
behaviours.given: accounts 'A' and 'B' each hold 10000, and 5000 has been withdrawn from 'A'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and 'B' has a balance of 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is shared across the ledger, so it is refused with 'daily-limit' and 'B' stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the limit is per customer and 'B' can only withdraw 0 more today

behaviours.title: The funds check is applied before the daily-limit check
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 and nothing has been withdrawn
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -5900

behaviours.title: A refused withdrawal's txnId can be reused later to succeed
behaviours.given: account 'A' held 100, a withdrawal of 150 with txnId 'w1' was refused, then 100 more was deposited (balance 200)
behaviours.when: 150 is withdrawn from 'A' with txnId 'w1' again
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 50
behaviours.contrary_then: 'w1' is remembered as already seen, the call returns ok but nothing is withdrawn and the balance stays 200
contrary_alternatives: the retry is refused with a 'duplicate' reason and the balance stays 200

behaviours.title: A transfer of 0 is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.when: 0 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'A' has only its deposit entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero transfer is accepted and recorded as a transfer-out entry on 'A'
contrary_alternatives: the zero transfer is silently accepted with no entries

behaviours.title: A negative transfer is refused as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 and 'B' holds 100
behaviours.when: -30 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }; 'A' stays 100 and 'B' stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer goes through in reverse: 'A' becomes 130 and 'B' becomes 70
contrary_alternatives: 30 is moved from 'A' to 'B' as if positive

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId reports success but moves nothing more
behaviours.given: account 'A' held 100 and 40 was transferred to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.when: 40 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' again with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'A' stays 60 and 'B' stays 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied twice: 'A' becomes 20 and 'B' becomes 80
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is refused with a 'duplicate' reason and balances stay 60 and 40

behaviours.title: Transferring more than the sender holds is refused as insufficient-funds
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 and 'B' holds 0
behaviours.when: 150 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; 'A' stays 100 and 'B' stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted: 'A' becomes -50 and 'B' becomes 150
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is moved: 'A' becomes 0 and 'B' becomes 100

behaviours.title: Transferring the whole balance is allowed and records out/in entries
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 and 'B' was never opened
behaviours.when: 100 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'A' is 0, 'B' is 100, 'A' gets a transfer-out entry of 100 and 'B' gets a transfer-in entry of 100, both with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is refused with 'insufficient-funds' because it would empty 'A'; 'A' stays 100 and 'B' 0
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is refused because 'B' was never opened

behaviours.title: Transfers are not subject to the 5000 daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000
behaviours.when: 6000 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'A' is 4000 and 'B' is 6000
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is refused with 'daily-limit' and 'A' stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: only 5000 is moved and the rest is refused

behaviours.title: Transfers do not use up the daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and 3000 was transferred from 'A' to 'B'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and 'A' is 2000
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer counted towards the limit, so the withdrawal is refused with 'daily-limit' and 'A' stays 7000
contrary_alternatives: only 2000 more may be withdrawn today

behaviours.title: Transfer amounts are rounded to cents, half a cent rounding up
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 1
behaviours.when: 0.125 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: 'B' receives 0.13 and both entries record 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent is dropped and 'B' receives 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the unrounded 0.125 is moved

behaviours.title: A refused transfer still opens the receiving account with no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where neither 'A' nor 'B' was opened
behaviours.when: 10 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; 'B' has balance 0 and entries('B') is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is refused with reason 'unknown-account'
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is accepted: 'A' becomes -10 and 'B' becomes 10

behaviours.title: A transfer to the same account leaves the balance unchanged but records two entries
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100
behaviours.when: 50 is transferred from 'A' to 'A' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 100, and 'A' gains a transfer-out and a transfer-in entry of 50 in that order
behaviours.contrary_then: the self-transfer is refused and 'A' keeps only its deposit entry
contrary_alternatives: the self-transfer is accepted as a no-op with no entries recorded
